question: Why do we study occupational health risks in nursing?

options.A: To help nurses stay safe and maintain a healthy career
options.B: To reduce the financial expenses of the hospital management
options.C: To eliminate all physical tasks from daily nursing duties
options.D: To ensure patients recover faster from their illnesses

explanation: Spotting workplace hazards early helps you protect your own health so you can enjoy a long, injury-free nursing journey. You matter too! [learn more](GNS122_U3_T7#GNS122_U3_T7_h1)

question: Why must a nurse pay attention to workplace hazards even if they currently feel strong and healthy?

options.A: Because infectious diseases disappear once they are identified
options.B: Because patients expect nurses to know about building safety
options.C: Because early awareness prevents future injury and chronic illness
options.D: Because hospital laws require passing a test every month

explanation: Many workplace risks cause slow, quiet damage over years of practice. Knowing the dangers now keeps you protected down the road. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T7#GNS122_U3_T7_h1)

question: Which disease is most commonly caught through accidental needle stick injuries in the clinic?
explanation: Hepatitis B is very easily spread through contaminated sharps in the hospital. This is why safety with needles is a huge deal for every nurse! [learn more](GNS122_U3_T7#GNS122_U3_T7_h2)

question: How do airborne germs mainly travel from one person to another?

options.A: Through direct contact with contaminated wound dressings
options.B: Through drinking unboiled water from hospital taps
options.C: Through tiny respiratory droplets suspended in the air
options.D: Through sharing unwashed eating utensils at the nurses station

explanation: Airborne pathogens hitch a ride on microscopic moisture droplets that float in the air and can be breathed in by anyone nearby. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T7#GNS122_U3_T7_h2)

question: Why are chemotherapy drugs considered dangerous for the nurses who handle them?

options.A: They always emit a poisonous gas that fills the entire hospital ward
options.B: They are designed to kill cells and can harm the nurse's cellular health
options.C: They cause immediate fainting if the nurse smells them
options.D: They instantly burn through standard hospital uniforms and skin

explanation: Chemo drugs work by destroying cells. That makes them powerful treatments for patients, but it also means nurses must handle them with extreme care to avoid toxic exposure. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T7#GNS122_U3_T7_h3)

question: What is a common cause of latex allergies among healthcare workers?

options.A: Drinking contaminated water from hospital supply pipes
options.B: Touching metal instruments sterilized in chemical baths
options.C: Repeated skin exposure to natural rubber proteins in gloves
options.D: Inhaling powder from standard surgical face masks

explanation: Wearing rubber gloves all day exposes your skin to natural proteins over and over, which can sensitize your immune system and trigger allergies over time. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T7#GNS122_U3_T7_h3)

question: What is the leading cause of ongoing back pain and injuries among nursing staff?

options.A: Writing patient reports while sitting on unadjusted chairs
options.B: Walking across slippery hospital floors in soft shoes
options.C: Lifting and moving heavy patients without proper mechanical assistance
options.D: Standing still at the nursing station during long night shifts

explanation: Pulling or lifting heavy patients manually puts massive strain on your lower back. Always use proper leverage, help, or lifting devices! [learn more](GNS122_U3_T7#GNS122_U3_T7_h4)

question: You need to move a heavy patient from a stretcher to a bed. What is the safest move?

options.A: Ask the patient to jump across while you hold their hands
options.B: Use a mechanical lift and ask another colleague to help
options.C: Pull the patient quickly using your arm muscles alone
options.D: Bend your back completely straight to gain extra lifting power

explanation: Teamwork and mechanical aids save your back! Never try to lift a heavy patient all by yourself. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T7#GNS122_U3_T7_h4)

question: Which protective gear is a must-have when working near an active X-ray machine?
explanation: Lead aprons and thyroid shields act like a block, stopping harmful radiation from reaching your sensitive organs and tissues. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T7#GNS122_U3_T7_h5)

question: Why is little-by-little exposure to radiation dangerous for healthcare workers over time?

options.A: It makes the nurse feel dizzy immediately after entering the room
options.B: It can cause gradual tissue damage and cellular mutations over years
options.C: It weakens the bones within a few minutes of standing nearby
options.D: It instantly heats up the skin and causes severe third-degree burns

explanation: Radiation adds up in the body over your career. That's why wearing your lead shield every single time is so important. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T7#GNS122_U3_T7_h5)

question: What do we call the emotional exhaustion and loss of care caused by long-term stress at work?
explanation: Burnout is real in demanding fields like nursing. It's that feeling of complete mental and emotional tiredness from too much stress. Take care of your mental health! [learn more](GNS122_U3_T7#GNS122_U3_T7_h6)

question: Which of these is NOT the right way to handle workplace violence in a hospital?

options.A: Using de-escalation techniques to calm an agitated patient
options.B: Ensuring an easy exit route is available during a patient interview
options.C: Accepting physical abuse quietly because it is part of the job
options.D: Reporting all threatening incidents to hospital security and management

explanation: Violence is never part of the job description. If someone threatens or abuses you, report it and use your hospital's security protocols immediately. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T7#GNS122_U3_T7_h6)

question: When should standard precautions be used in clinical practice?

options.A: Only when blood or body fluid is visibly staining the bedsheets
options.B: To every patient, regardless of their diagnosis or infection status
options.C: Strictly during surgical procedures in the main operating theatre
options.D: Only when caring for patients with known infectious diseases

explanation: Treat every patient as potentially infectious. Standard precautions keep you and everyone around you safe from hidden germs. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T7#GNS122_U3_T7_h7)

question: Why are nurses strongly advised NOT to recap used needles?

options.A: It violates hospital rules regarding plastic waste recycling
options.B: It drastically increases the risk of accidental needle stick injuries
options.C: It damages the sharp tip making it useless for the next patient
options.D: It wastes valuable nursing time during busy medication rounds

explanation: Trying to guide a tiny cap back onto a used needle is one of the quickest ways to accidentally poke yourself. Drop it straight into the safety box instead! [learn more](GNS122_U3_T7#GNS122_U3_T7_h7)

question: What is the main purpose of wearing Personal Protective Equipment (PPE)?

options.A: To create a physical barrier between the nurse and infectious hazards
options.B: To hide the nurse's facial expressions from anxious family members
options.C: To comply with fashion trends established by hospital management
options.D: To keep the nurse's personal clothing clean from everyday dust

explanation: PPE acts like your personal shield, stopping germs, chemicals, and fluids from touching your skin or clothes. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T7#GNS122_U3_T7_h8)

question: Why is taking off your PPE in the correct, specific order so important?

options.A: To ensure the equipment can be washed and reused for the next shift
options.B: To prevent transferring trapped pathogens from the gear onto your skin
options.C: To prevent the plastic straps from snapping during disposal
options.D: To speed up the process so you can leave the isolation room faster

explanation: The outside of your PPE is covered in germs. If you take it off carelessly, you'll end up wiping those germs right onto your face or hands! [learn more](GNS122_U3_T7#GNS122_U3_T7_h8)

question: Who has the primary legal duty to provide a safe working environment in a hospital?

options.A: The pharmaceutical companies supplying hospital medications
options.B: The individual nursing students on clinical placement
options.C: The patients admitted to the medical and surgical wards
options.D: The hospital management and institutional administration

explanation: Management is legally required to give you safe facilities, working gear, and proper protection so you can do your job without undue risk. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T7#GNS122_U3_T7_h9)

question: What is your responsibility as a nurse regarding hospital safety rules?

options.A: To follow protocols, report hazards, and participate in safety training
options.B: To rewrite hospital rulebooks whenever a new patient is admitted
options.C: To purchase safety equipment using personal financial funds
options.D: To inspect all electrical wiring in the building every weekend

explanation: Safety is a team effort! Following guidelines and speaking up when something is broken helps keep both you and your patients out of harm's way. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T7#GNS122_U3_T7_h9)
